final_answer:
Depth-first search (DFS) explores as far as possible along each branch before backtracking, while breadth-first search (BFS) explores all neighbors at the current depth before moving to the next level.  

DFS uses a stack (or recursion) for implementation, whereas BFS uses a queue.  

DFS is better for finding a path in a maze or exploring all possible paths, while BFS is better for finding the shortest path in an unweighted graph.  

Choose DFS when memory is limited or when the solution is deep in the graph, and choose BFS when the shortest path is needed or the graph is wide.  

DFS might miss the shortest path, but BFS guarantees the shortest path in unweighted graphs.  

Both have their use cases depending on the problem structure and requirements.
